comments.text:
Load/save dispatcher.
Purpose: select the save path when A=$53 and the load path otherwise, then perform the KERNAL file operation and restore game state.
Inputs: A is the command character; filename and state buffers are already prepared.
Outputs: saved or loaded state; runtime vectors and display state restored.
Assumptions: KERNAL ROM and I/O can be banked in.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, KERNAL workspace.
Hardware changes: switches $01 banking and calls KERNAL PLOT, SETLFS, SETNAM, LOAD/SAVE.

SERIALIZE_ALL_OBJECT_FLAGS ($05D8-$062E)
Purpose: walk every area and variable-size object record during save/load, copying exactly one mutable flags byte per object between the live database and save buffer.
Inputs: mode selected by LOAD_SAVE_DISPATCH; area table based at $9D00; object count/record size fields; save-buffer cursor.
Outputs: save writes 546 object flag bytes to $8836-$8A57; load restores each record byte 0 from the same span.
Assumptions: 34 area records are traversed in pointer-table order and record byte +8 is total size.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, pointer/counter scratch and destination/source cursors.
Hardware changes: none directly; the caller performs KERNAL banking and file I/O.

SELECT_NEXT_AREA_OBJECT_LIST ($05EC-$0617)
Purpose: read the next database-relative area pointer and initialize that area's object-list cursor for serialization.
Inputs: area-pointer table $7A/$7B, table index Y, and database base $109C/$109D.
Outputs: installs first-object pointer $7E/$7F, object count $0411, and saved table index $0413.
Assumptions: table words are little-endian direct offsets from the database base; area byte +1 is object count and the first object begins at +8.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $7E/$7F, $0411, and $0413.
Hardware changes: none.

ADVANCE_TO_NEXT_SERIALIZED_OBJECT ($0618-$062E)
Purpose: advance the serialization cursor to the next variable-length object and decrement the current area's remaining count.
Inputs: object pointer $7E/$7F, remaining count $0411, and saved area-table index $0413.
Outputs: advances $7E/$7F by record byte +8, decrements $0411, restores Y from $0413, and leaves Z set exactly when the count reaches zero.
Assumptions: record byte +8 is the total record size.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $7E/$7F, and $0411.
Hardware changes: none.

KERNAL-vector restoration bridge.
Purpose: copy the 32-byte canonical vector table from KERNAL ROM $FD30-$FD4F to RAM $0314-$0333, then install CHROUT=$86CF and NMI=$7579.
Inputs: standard C64 KERNAL ROM.
Outputs: restored RAM vectors, custom output/NMI hooks, sprites disabled.
Assumptions: $01=$37 selects KERNAL ROM and I/O.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags.
Hardware changes: masks IRQs during the copy, writes $01, $0314-$0333, and VIC sprite-enable $D015.

Castle SID data map ($065A-$1046), byte-identical to the PSID payload at load address $065A. Frequency low/high tables are $065A-$06B9/$06BA-$0719; pattern streams $071A-$0D06; split pattern pointers $0D07/$0D3C (53 each); 51 tune/voice order pointers $0D71-$0DD6; order streams $0DD7-$0F14; eight 9-byte instruments $0F15-$0F5C; packed pitch/effect records $0F5E-$0FDD; vibrato/control/offset tables $0FE2-$1046. Boundaries and consumers are verified from the original player and independent PSID payload.

Gameplay event dispatch state. EVENT_OBJECT_ID $1082 identifies the triggering object. ACTIVE_EVENT_MASK $1084 uses bit 0 collided/movement, bit 3 timer, bit 2 shot and bit 1 activated; PENDING_EVENT_MASK $1085 is promoted/consumed by the frame path. UPDATE_FRAME_INPUT_EVENTS produces these fields and DISPATCH_FRAME_CONDITIONS selects FCL tokens from them. Verified from exact producers and all four interpreter event tests.

Geometry-update consequences. PENDING_CRUSH_CHECK $1086 requests a scan after ordinary geometry becomes visible. PENDING_SUPPORT_CHECK $1087 requests a support/fall pass after geometry becomes invisible. CHECK_NEWLY_VISIBLE_CRUSH and DROP_PLAYER_TO_SUPPORT consume them. SENSOR_COUNT_REBUILT $1099 is rebuilt by rendering and copied to ACTIVE_SENSOR_COUNT $109A for periodic strength drain.

Little-endian work-buffer pointer initialized to $87CC. The renderer uses that storage as its 120x30-byte linear pixel buffer. LOAD_SAVE_DISPATCH reuses the same base for its 652-byte serialized payload, then advances its private cursor to end-exclusive $8A58 before KERNAL SAVE. The user-defined DATA reference records this exact pointer value without changing the byte typing.

Castle sound/music menu state, not a hardware-enable register. SOUND_MENU_STATE $123B is toggled by the information menu and mirrored to SOUND_GATE_STATE $123A. SID_INITIALIZE_IF_ENABLED runs a request only when $123A is zero; nonzero returns. The IRQ/player state mirrors this gate as needed.

Raw control collection. RAW_CONTROL_COUNT $1379 bounds at five; RAW_CONTROL_CODES $137A onward holds active joystick/keyboard codes. READ_CONTROL_INPUT produces them from CIA 1. UPDATE_FRAME_INPUT_EVENTS translates them through CONTROL_ACTION_MAP $1382-$13AD.

CONTROL_ACTION_MAP ($1382-$13AD)
Purpose: 22 raw-code/action pairs shared by keyboard and joystick.
Exact mapping: ^,*,$91 -> action 3; =,$92 -> 4; Z,$93 -> 5; X,$94 -> 6; P -> 7; L -> 8; C -> 9; W -> 10; R -> 11; F -> 12; U -> 13; + -> 21; 1,$95 -> 22; A -> 27; Space -> 30; I -> 41.
Consumer: UPDATE_FRAME_INPUT_EVENTS at $48C1-$48E2.
Evidence: all 44 bytes observed and dispatch comparisons verified.

FCL_TOKEN_LENGTHS ($13AE-$13DE)
Purpose: maps low-six-bit FCL opcodes 0-48 to complete token lengths, including the selector/opcode byte.
Inputs: X=opcode when read by EXECUTE_FCL_STREAM.
Outputs: length byte; zero denotes an unsupported/non-advancing opcode in this Castle build.
Assumptions: FCL token = event selector in bits 7-6 plus opcode in bits 5-0.
Evidence: all 193 parsed streams and 809 tokens consume their declared bounds exactly.

OBJECT_BASE_SIZE_BY_TYPE ($13DF-$13ED)
Purpose: maps object type 0-14 to the fixed record size before optional residual FCL bytecode.
Values: 9,12,14,10,16,16,16,16,16,16,16,19,22,25,28.
Use: residual length = record[8] - table[type]; residual stream starts at record + table[type].
Assumptions: type is the low nybble of record byte 0.

riddle_ptrs_13ee ($13EE-$13FF). Nine little-endian pointers selected by FCL print values $80-$88 after masking to 0-8. Values in selector order: $1B29,$18AE,$1908,$194B,$1990,$19DE,$1A3B,$1A81,$1AEC. Consumer $6DB1-$6DB9. This is not a terminator for the following message table.

fixed_messages_1400 ($1400-$17DF). Exactly 62 fixed 16-byte records {control/blanking flag, 15 glyph bytes}; FCL ordinary message n uses $1410 + 16*(n-1). First record is 00 followed by ` DUALIS-CRACK! `. Exact stride/consumer contradict the former 75 terminator-record interpretation.

Active-language UI records ($17E0-$1883). Starts with six 11-byte strength labels, followed by the 23-byte information-menu command line, keys/spirits/strength labels, and three fixed 16-byte count/score templates. Digits at $1856/$1857, $1866/$1867, and $187C-$1882 are mutable display fields.
save_prompts_1884 ($1884-$18AD). Three fixed 14-byte records {control,13 glyphs}: `TAPE OR DISC `, `(T/D) ? #    `, and filename prompt. $189B is patched with the chosen device letter.

riddles_18ae ($18AE-$1B76). Nine structured records reached through riddle_ptrs_13ee. Each is {line_count; line...}; a normal line is {x_advance,y,printable_size,control,glyphs}. Size $FF has no payload and draws the 21-asterisk template at $1C4E. Parser $6DC3-$6E3E verifies every boundary.
linear_row_ptrs_1c75 ($1C75-$1D64). 120 little-endian row pointers; entry n is exactly $87CC + 30*n. Generic blitter $7CF6-$7FDB, rectangular copy $7FE6, and HUD/text callers consume them.
bitmap_hud_ptrs_1d65 ($1D65-$1DD8). 58 little-endian pointers into non-contiguous VIC bitmap/HUD locations, consumed by $7FE6 and HUD routines $702C-$72D9.

packed_hud_graphics_1dd9 ($1DD9-$2036). Generic records begin with five-byte header {row_bytes,row_count,last_byte_mask,frame_stride_lo,frame_stride_hi}, followed by packed two-bit pixels. Exact record starts: $1DD9,$1E32,$1E45,$1E8A,$1E9F,$1F49,$1F6F,$1FB0; the final record has 13 structurally verified 10-byte frames. Low seven selector bits choose frame; bit 7 selects alternate compositing. Individual icon meanings are inferred from callers, while format/bounds are verified.
raster_frames_2038 ($2038-$20F7). Eight 24-byte raster/HUD animation frames. IRQ path $74C8-$7520 copies phase pairs to multicolor bitmap destinations $E128 and $E268.

background_edge_masks_20f8 ($20F8-$21F9). 86 three-byte mask records selected as X=3*$4B8C by $4D90, then AND/OR composited into each linear-framebuffer row. Artistic identities are inferred; record format and consumer are observed.
area1_background_texture_21fa ($21FA-$2319). Eighteen 16-byte texture/rotation records for the special area-1 background. $4CF6-$4D8F selects/rotates row patterns from yaw $2411&7.

compact_font_231a ($231A-$2405). 59 glyphs for ASCII $20-$5A, four source bytes each. Text renderer $85E1-$863F expands each source bit nybble to multicolor bitmap pixels. $2406 is the separate $EA save-state marker/alignment byte, not font payload.

SAVE_STATE_MARKER begins the 106-byte mutable engine-state span $2406-$246F. Marker $EA validates loaded files. LOAD_SAVE_DISPATCH copies this span to $87CC-$8835, then SERIALIZE_ALL_OBJECT_FLAGS appends 546 record flag bytes at $8836-$8A57. Total payload is 652 bytes ($028C), end-exclusive $8A58; a PRG container adds load address $87CC for a 654-byte file.

Player pose in little-endian 16-bit world coordinates: X $2407/$2408, vertical/Y $2409/$240A, Z $240B/$240C. MOVE_STEP_SCALED $240D/$240E and MOVE_STEP_RAW $240F feed translation. VIEW_PITCH $2410 and VIEW_YAW $2411 wrap in the $00-$47 (72-step) angular domain. Verified from trig-table, movement, entrance and collision use.

Player stance/collision dimensions. PLAYER_HEIGHT_UNITS $2412 is inferred from crawl transitions and stand-up adjustment. PLAYER_HEIGHT_SCALED $2413 is verified in collision/fall calculations. FALL_DAMAGE_THRESHOLD $2414 equals 2*CURRENT_AREA_SCALE; MAX_FLOOR_STEP $2415 equals 1*scale; CURRENT_AREA_SCALE is $2416. The threshold roles supersede the earlier generic collision-extent names.

FCL_VARIABLE_BASE. Castle condition bytecode addresses variables as $2438+index. The live high variables are score $2442-$2444, spirits destroyed $2454 (v28), strength/shield $2455 (v29), movement mode $2456 (v30), key count $2457 (v31), and pending key ID $2458 (v32).

Unsigned 24-bit little-endian score at $2442-$2444. ADD_SCORE_U24 propagates carry across all three bytes; FORMAT_UNSIGNED_DECIMAL and menu/HUD paths display seven decimal digits. First area visits add 17,500 ($00445C); collected keys add 125,000 ($01E848).

Castle Master game-state variables exposed to Freescape condition bytecode. $2454 is FCL variable 28, spirits destroyed; $2455 is variable 29, strength/shield; $2456 is variable 30, movement mode; $2457 is variable 31, keys collected; $2458 is variable 32, pending key ID. The spirits-meter update computes elapsed * (21 - destroyed) / 21 and triggers completion when the normalized result reaches 64.

Thunder/lightning scheduler. LIGHTNING_COUNTDOWN $2459 is decremented by LIGHTNING_DIVIDER $2468 (reload 60). Zero reseeds to ($1C64 & $3F)+10; outdoors this requests sound 8, flashes VIC border/background white for one interrupt interval, restores area colors and requests redraw. Count 1 incorporates the lightning graphic, then becomes zero. This is not gameplay time.

Aim and periodic state. AIM_SELECTOR_X/Y are $2465/$2466 and AIM_MODE_ENABLED is $2467. LIGHTNING_DIVIDER $2468 reloads 60. PERIODIC_TICK_DIVIDER $2469 reloads 10 and increments CURRENT_TIMER_TICK $246D; comparison with PREVIOUS_TIMER_TICK $246C raises the FCL timer event. SPIRITS_METER_ELAPSED $246A increments on the longer IRQ divider.

MUL_S16_S8_TO_S24 ($2470-$24FD)
Purpose: multiply a signed 16-bit value by a signed 8-bit value using shift/add arithmetic.
Inputs: signed factor in A low/X high, signed factor in Y, and interrupt-state convention byte $1C72.
Outputs: signed 24-bit product in $82-$84.
Assumptions: binary two's-complement operands; $1C72 accurately says whether the engine already owns the interrupt-disabled arithmetic critical section.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $82-$8C, and sign scratch $1056.
Hardware changes: executes SEI; executes CLI before return only when $1C72=0, otherwise leaves interrupts disabled; no VIC-II, SID, or CIA register changes.

MUL_S16_S16_TO_S32 ($24FE-$259C)
Purpose: multiply two signed 16-bit values using magnitude conversion and shift/add arithmetic.
Inputs: signed factors in $88/$89 and $8C/$8D.
Outputs: signed 32-bit product in $82-$85; zero input produces zero output through the fast path.
Assumptions: binary two's-complement operands and writable shared arithmetic workspace.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $82-$8D including operand work bytes, and sign scratch $1056; Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: none.

DIV_S24_BY_S16 ($259F-$2642)
Purpose: divide a signed 24-bit dividend by a signed 16-bit divisor using restoring long division.
Inputs: dividend in A low/X middle/Y high; divisor in $8C/$8D.
Outputs: signed quotient in $88-$8A and signed remainder in $82-$84.
Assumptions: binary two's-complement operands; divisor is nonzero. This routine has no divide-by-zero guard, so zero is an invalid caller state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $82-$8D, and self-held sign bytes $259D/$259E.
Hardware changes: none.

MUL_S8_S8_TO_S16 ($2643-$26AA)
Purpose: multiply two signed 8-bit values using shift/add arithmetic.
Inputs: signed factors in X and Y.
Outputs: signed 16-bit product in $82/$83; zero input produces zero output through the fast path.
Assumptions: binary two's-complement operands and writable shared arithmetic workspace.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $82-$88, $8C, and sign scratch $1056.
Hardware changes: none.

DIV_S32_BY_S16 ($26AB-$274C)
Purpose: divide a signed 32-bit dividend by a signed 16-bit divisor using restoring long division.
Inputs: dividend in $88-$8B and divisor in $8C/$8D.
Outputs: signed quotient in $88-$8B and unsigned-magnitude remainder in $82/$83. A zero dividend returns zero immediately; a zero divisor also returns early without a meaningful quotient and is an invalid caller state.
Assumptions: binary two's-complement operands; valid callers provide a nonzero divisor.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $82-$8D, and sign scratch $1056.
Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Render and present one scene when dirty/effect state requires it.
Inputs: effect $1086, dirty flags $1059/$105A, object-list roots $1060-$1062 and $242A-$242C.
Outputs: rendered/presented scene, sensor count $1099, and status update through $72DA.
Assumptions: bounds, matrix, traversal, painter-sort, draw, HUD and presentation routines.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and renderer scratch; changes bitmap/screen/color memory through callees but no SID/CIA state directly.
Hardware changes: Writes renderer buffers and VIC-visible bitmap, screen, and color memory through callees; no direct SID or CIA access.

Purpose: Traverse one variable-size Freescape object list.
Inputs: X=count and $80/$81=first record; record byte 8 supplies the next size.
Outputs: visible geometry queued for drawing and sensor count $1099. Type 0 and flag $40 skip; type 2 counts a sensor; type 1 dispatches cube, type 3 rectangle, types 4..9 pyramid, and >=10 line/polygon.
Assumptions: coarse bounds unless bypass $2417.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $7A/$7B, $80/$81 and local self-modified scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Hardware changes: None directly.

Purpose: Compute coarse view bounds for object rejection.
Inputs: 72-step pitch/yaw $2410/$2411, camera/player coordinates $2407-$240C, and bypass flag $2417.
Outputs: six signed axis min/max bounds $1089-$108E.
Assumptions: VIEW_OCTANT_BOUNDS_DISPATCH.
Clobbers: A, X, flags and scratch $2940/$2941; no C64 hardware registers are changed. It samples four view-corner octants, then translates remaining open bounds by camera position; coarse AABB/octant-frustum wording is descriptive, while the bounds algorithm is exact.
Hardware changes: None.

Self-modified eight-way coarse-bound dispatch.
Purpose: transfer to the octant-specific initializer selected by the current pitch/yaw quadrant.
Inputs: $2A0B/$2A11 have written this JMP operand from VIEW_OCTANT_BOUNDS_DISPATCH using the index derived at $2A04-$2A07.
Outputs: control enters one of SET_VIEW_BOUNDS_CASE_0..7, which initializes the applicable coarse bounds before FINISH_VIEW_BOUNDS_SAMPLES.
Assumptions: the dispatch table contains eight valid resident targets and this RAM operand is writable; captured $FFFF is only the pre-patch placeholder.
Clobbers: none at the JMP itself; the selected initializer clobbers A and flags.
Hardware changes: None.
Eight little-endian destinations selected by the self-modified JMP at $2A14. Each entry initializes one coarse world/frustum bound combination before the common continuation at $2AB4.

BUILD_CUBOID_CAMERA_BASIS ($2B4A-$2C72)
Purpose: transform a cuboid's lower corner and three axis extents into a camera-space origin plus three edge vectors.
Inputs: relative bounds through $10AA/$10AB, active object record $108F/$1090, and view matrix $106C-$1074.
Outputs: transformed origin $003E-$0043 and transformed edge vectors $0002-$0013.
Assumptions: type-1 record extents are bytes +4 through +6 and matrix coefficients use scale 64.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $80-$84, $B0-$B5, and geometry workspace.
Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Build the fixed-point view/projection matrix.
Inputs: pitch/yaw $2410/$2411, trig table $123C-$12CB with 72 sin/cos pairs at 5-degree spacing and scale 64, identity $2C73-$2C7B, and aspect/depth diagonal $2C7C-$2C84=(40,64,32).
Outputs: view matrix $106C-$1074.
Assumptions: MULTIPLY_3X3_FIXED_MATRICES.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and matrix scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Hardware changes: None.

QUEUE_CUBOID_OBJECT ($2D20-$2F20)
Purpose: expand a cuboid's eight vertices, reject it against the view volume, select visible face colors, and project/clip/append surviving faces.
Inputs: active object record $108F/$1090, camera-basis inputs, object ID $105C, side mask $1055, and packed face colors.
Outputs: appends surviving faces to the visible queue and updates count $106A, or appends nothing when rejected or colorless.
Assumptions: the type-1 record and cuboid topology templates at $12CC+ are valid.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02-$6D, $80-$84, $1055, and clip/project/queue scratch.
Hardware changes: none.

QUEUE_PYRAMID_OBJECT ($2F21-$32DE)
Purpose: construct orientation-specific pyramid vertices/faces, reject them, select packed colors, and project/clip/queue surviving faces.
Inputs: active record, object type $1068 for types 4-9, relative bounds, view matrix, player-relative workspace, and side mask $1055.
Outputs: appends surviving visible queue entries or nothing after rejection.
Assumptions: the type 4-9 record, its four ordinate bytes, and topology tables are valid.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, zero-page vertex workspace, self-held counters, and clip/project/queue state.
Hardware changes: none.

QUEUE_EXPLICIT_LINE_OR_POLYGON_OBJECT ($32E1-$33A1)
Purpose: decode explicit vertices, convert them to player-relative coordinates, reject/transform them, and queue a line or polygon.
Inputs: record $108F/$1090, type $1068, color byte +9, coordinate triples beginning at +10, and player pose $2407-$240C.
Outputs: sets vertex count $10B0=type-8 and appends the transformed/projected queue entry, using line mode for two vertices.
Assumptions: types 10-14 encode two through six vertices with three coordinate bytes per vertex.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02+, $7A/$7B, $82/$83, mutable bytes $32DF/$32E0, and render scratch.
Hardware changes: none.

QUEUE_RECTANGLE_OBJECT ($33A3-$3488)
Purpose: construct the appropriate four-corner planar rectangle from object bounds, select its relevant color side, and project/clip/queue it.
Inputs: bounds through $10AA/$10AB, active record $108F/$1090, side mask $1055, and packed color byte +9.
Outputs: appends one visible quad entry or nothing after rejection/color testing.
Assumptions: a type-3 record has one zero extent identifying its plane.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02-$19, $7A-$7D, mutable byte $33A2, and clip/project/queue scratch.
Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Painter-sort visible 4-byte entries with adjacent bubble passes.
Inputs: queued entries and their world AABBs.
Outputs: stable draw order after per-axis relations are packed into 2-bit codes; codes $02,$08,$20,$0A,$22,$28,$2A keep order, all others swap until stable. This is an overlap-based painter algorithm with no z-buffer.
Assumptions: Caller-established pointers, counts, tables, and scratch state described in Inputs are valid.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and compare/swap scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: Draw the sorted visible queue.
Inputs: painter-sorted face/object commands.
Outputs: complete linear frame buffer after background $4B91, polygon spans $4411 or line spans $45E8, and fill $3F76.
Assumptions: queue records are valid.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and renderer scratch; writes frame-buffer memory but no SID/CIA state.
Hardware changes: Writes ordinary renderer frame-buffer RAM; no direct SID or CIA access.

Purpose: Present the completed frame.
Inputs: linear viewport and state $1064.
Outputs: color cells through $61A8 when selected, normal bitmap blit through $4B24, or alternate transition/effect through $82E3.
Assumptions: renderer buffers are complete.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and presentation scratch; changes VIC-visible bitmap/screen/color memory through callees.
Hardware changes: Writes VIC-visible bitmap, screen, and color memory through callees.

Purpose: Multiply two 3x3 signed fixed-point matrices.
Inputs: matrices through caller-established internal pointer/state.
Outputs: a 3x3 result, accumulating products then rounding and rescaling by 64.
Assumptions: MUL_S8_S8_TO_S16.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $82-$84/$88/$8C and loop/pointer scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Hardware changes: None.

TRANSFORM_VERTICES_TO_CAMERA_SPACE ($3730-$37AE)
Purpose: apply the current 3x3 fixed-point view matrix to caller-prepared vertex triples.
Inputs: vertex count $10B0, caller-established source/global pointer and coordinate workspace, and matrix $106C-$1074.
Outputs: signed 16-bit camera-space x/y/z triples at $003E onward with six-byte stride; dot products are divided by 64.
Assumptions: the caller has already prepared the source coordinates, including any viewer-relative translation; the count fits the fixed work buffer and matrix coefficients use scale 64.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $B0-$B5, $82-$84, multiplication scratch, and the destination workspace.
Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Dispatch one polygon-edge intersection to the active view-volume plane.
Inputs: X selects the edge/vertex slot and $104B is plane number 1..5.
Outputs: the selected routine writes an intersection point and restores X before returning.
Assumptions: CLIP_PLANE_INTERSECTION_DISPATCH plus signed multiply $24FE and divide $26AB.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags and clipper/math scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed. $37BC/$37C2 patch JMP $37C5.
Hardware changes: None.

Self-modified five-way clip-plane intersection dispatch.
Purpose: transfer to the edge-intersection routine for the active view-volume plane.
Inputs: $37BC/$37C2 have written this JMP operand from CLIP_PLANE_INTERSECTION_DISPATCH using plane selector $104B; X selects the edge/vertex slot.
Outputs: control enters the selected intersection routine, which writes the crossing point and returns to the shared polygon clipper.
Assumptions: selector $104B is 1..5, the dispatch table contains valid resident targets, and this RAM operand is writable; captured $FFFF is only the pre-patch placeholder.
Clobbers: none at the JMP itself; the selected routine clobbers A, X, Y, flags, and clipper/math scratch while preserving the calling convention.
Hardware changes: None.
Five little-endian entry points selected by the self-modified JMP at $37C5. Each routine clips/intersects an edge against one view-volume plane and returns to the shared polygon clipper.

Purpose: Intersect a crossing polygon edge with plane x+z=0.
Inputs: X selects endpoint records in signed 16-bit camera-coordinate arrays.
Outputs: interpolated crossing point written back to the clipper work arrays, with x+z constrained to zero.
Assumptions: signed multiply $24FE and divide $26AB; clobbers A, X, Y, flags and zero-page clipper/math scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and routine scratch as used by the implementation.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: Intersect a crossing polygon edge with plane y+z=0.
Inputs: X selects endpoint records in signed 16-bit camera-coordinate arrays.
Outputs: interpolated crossing point written back to the clipper work arrays, with y+z constrained to zero.
Assumptions: signed multiply $24FE and divide $26AB; clobbers A, X, Y, flags and zero-page clipper/math scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and routine scratch as used by the implementation.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: Intersect a crossing polygon edge with plane z-x=0.
Inputs: X selects endpoint records in signed 16-bit camera-coordinate arrays.
Outputs: interpolated crossing point written back to the clipper work arrays, with z-x constrained to zero.
Assumptions: signed multiply $24FE and divide $26AB; clobbers A, X, Y, flags and zero-page clipper/math scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and routine scratch as used by the implementation.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: Intersect a crossing polygon edge with plane z-y=0.
Inputs: X selects endpoint records in signed 16-bit camera-coordinate arrays.
Outputs: interpolated crossing point written back to the clipper work arrays, with z-y constrained to zero.
Assumptions: signed multiply $24FE and divide $26AB; clobbers A, X, Y, flags and zero-page clipper/math scratch; no C64 hardware registers are changed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and routine scratch as used by the implementation.
Hardware changes: None.

Purpose: Intersect a crossing polygon edge with near plane z=0.

SID_UPDATE_ONE_VOICE ($CA11-$CF1A; command continuations $CF79-$CFBD)
Purpose: interpret one voice's order/pattern commands, select instrument/frequency, advance note/gate/duration and modulation state, and prepare the seven SID-register shadow bytes used by the outer tick.
Inputs: current voice $C809=0-2, SID register offset $C808=0/7/14, stream positions/pointers $C80A+ and $F7-$FC, and initialized player tables/state $C806-$C884.
Outputs: advances one voice's shadow bytes, counters, and pointers. Normal paths return through $CAE4/$CC7F/$CC9E/$CF1A. A global end marker clears $C806 and all three voice controls, deliberately discards its direct caller's return address, and exits the enclosing tick.
Assumptions: stream/table pointers and command encoding are valid; $CF1B-$CF78 is the separate SID initializer, while $CF79-$CFBD are noncontiguous command-tail continuations. Musical names for individual proprietary commands are not claimed without score tracing.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, extensive $C806-$C884 state, self-modified operands $CA55/$CF7C/$CF8B/$CFA6, dispatch bytes, and stack on global-end escape.
Hardware changes: command $A0 can clear selected voice control $D404 plus offset 0/7/14; global end clears $D404/$D40B/$D412. The outer tick $C885-$CA10 performs the normal $D400-$D418 flush.

SID_PLAYER_INITIALIZE ($CF1B-$CF78)
Purpose: reset the three-voice player and install the requested selector offset for subsequent SID ticks.
Inputs: A is the selector value; zero is valid for initialization/reset; resident SID tables and the $102F-$1046 seed state are installed.
Outputs: stores six times the selector in $C813; gate-pulses then clears all three voice-control registers; clears player state $C806-$C884 as encoded, restores seed bytes into $1017-$102E, initializes self-modified player pointers $F7-$FC, and leaves player state/volume byte $C806 and $C82C at $0F.
Assumptions: selector multiplication addresses the verified per-selector player layout; writable self-modifying and state storage is available.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $F7-$FC, $1017-$102E, and $C806-$C884; Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: writes $01 then $00 to SID voice-control registers $D404, $D40B, and $D412; it does not change SID master volume $D418.

SID_INITIALIZE_IF_ENABLED ($CFD8-$CFE3)
Purpose: request a one-shot sound only when the game's sound/music gate permits it.
Inputs: requested zero-based sound index in A; gate byte $123A.
Outputs: when $123A is zero, increments A to the player's one-based index and tail-calls SID initializer $CF1B; otherwise returns without changing the player.
Assumptions: callers use Castle's internal sound indexes.
Clobbers: X and, on the enabled path, registers/state clobbered by $CF1B.
Hardware changes: enabled path initializes SID player state; later ticks write $D400-$D418.
Evidence: branch, increment and tail transfer observed; caller sound identities independently verified.

vic_bitmap_e000 ($E000-$FF3F). Full 8,000-byte 320x200 multicolor bitmap selected by $D018. The centered 30x15-cell, 240x120-pixel viewport begins $E528. $FF40-$FF42 are return/padding bytes and are not bitmap data; copied interrupt dispatcher begins $FF43.

KERNAL_RESIDUE_FF43 ($FF43-$FF47) - inactive copied-KERNAL bytes, not executed by this occupant.
Classified data, not code. These five bytes are a verbatim copy of the KERNAL's pre-dispatch
sequence (PHP / PLA / AND #$EF / PHA) left in RAM by an earlier phase. In the captured menu
occupant nothing reaches them: they carry zero incoming references, and the only live entry into
the copied dispatcher is the hardware IRQ/BRK vector at $FFFE/$FFFF, which points directly at
$FF48. Modelling them as executable would assert a control-flow path the capture does not contain.
Banking: at the capture $01=$35, so $E000-$FFFF is RAM with KERNAL ROM banked out; these bytes are
physical RAM, and the same RAM is the VIC bank 3 multicolor bitmap ($E000-$FF3F) plus its tail.
See KERNAL_RESIDUE_FF5B for the rest of the residue and IRQ_DISPATCH for the live dispatcher.

IRQ_DISPATCH ($FF48-$FF5A)
Purpose: implement the copied KERNAL common IRQ/BRK dispatcher by saving A/X/Y, testing the stacked Break flag, and transferring through the appropriate RAM vector.
Inputs: a hardware IRQ/BRK frame or compatible synthetic frame on the stack; RAM vectors $0314/$0315 and $0316/$0317 are installed.
Outputs: jumps indirectly through $0316 for Break set or $0314 for Break clear after pushing A, X, and Y.
Assumptions: the selected handler follows the copied KERNAL convention and restores the three saved registers before RTI; physical RAM at $FF48 is the active occupant when KERNAL ROM is hidden.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and stack until the selected handler restores them.
Hardware changes: none directly; the all-RAM IRQ/BRK vector $FFFE/$FFFF points here.

KERNAL_RESIDUE_FF5B ($FF5B-$FF7F) - inactive copied-KERNAL bytes, not executed by this occupant.
Classified data, not code. Decoded as instructions these bytes read as the KERNAL's post-dispatch
tail (JSR $E518, raster wait on $D012, $D019 acknowledge, CIA 1 $DC0D/$DC0E setup, JMP $EE8E), but
every one of those targets lies inside $E000-$FF3F, which at this capture is the VIC bank 3
multicolor bitmap - image data, not routines. Disassembling them therefore manufactures call and
jump edges into pixels. Nothing in the captured occupant references this range.
Banking: $01=$35 banks RAM under BASIC and KERNAL while leaving I/O visible, so the CPU sees these
RAM bytes rather than KERNAL ROM. The program reaches genuine KERNAL routines only by first
setting $01=$37, after which the ROM's own jump table executes and these RAM bytes are irrelevant.

Copied KERNAL jump table ($FF81-$FFF5) - inactive RAM residue, classified data.
These bytes duplicate the KERNAL's documented entry table (CINT, IOINIT, SETMSG $FF90,
SETLFS $FFBA, SETNAM $FFBD, LOAD $FFD5, SAVE $FFD8, PLOT $FFF0, ...). They are NOT what executes
when the program calls those addresses. At this capture $01=$35, so $E000-$FFFF is RAM; a call to
$FFD5 in that state would run these RAM bytes, whose JMP operands point into $E000-$FF3F - the VIC
bank 3 multicolor bitmap. The program instead sets $01=$37 before any KERNAL call, banking ROM in
so the ROM's own table runs; these RAM copies are then invisible.
They are therefore kept as data with their public entry labels and per-entry contracts retained as
bank-qualified logical API annotations: the labels document where the program calls, and the
incoming references from the program are real, but no outgoing flow is asserted from these bytes.
The three-byte $6C xx 03 entries ($FFC0 OPEN, $FFC3 CLOSE, $FFCF CHRIN, $FFD2 CHROUT, ...) are
indirect through the $0300-$0332 RAM vector page and are likewise inert here.
